notes: Built from docs/library/cricket.md by scripts/build-padel-library.js; edit cricket.md, then rebuild. Same format as the padel library. Scores come from the existing scoring engine, unchanged. Words in curly brackets are filled in by the engine from the athlete's results; Gemini never writes or changes these lines. plain_name, measures and weapon (headline, body, evenness) are PeakPerformance wording added for the report, not text from cricket.md.
draft_notice_help: Shown in the footer of every page of the cricket athlete report. Set draft_notice to null (or "") to switch it off; applies to reports generated after the change. Kept when the library is rebuilt.

target.label: Gold
target.text: Tier target is the Gold line (score 75). Priorities are ranked by score points below 75, biggest gap first; ties keep library order.

plan.text: One combined 6-week plan: every selected fix runs from week 1. A fix shorter than 6 weeks switches to that test's maintain fix (where the library has one) for the remaining weeks.

tests.name: 10m Sprint
tests.what_we_measured: How fast you cover 10 metres from a standing start, about half the length of the pitch.
tests.notice: you call a quick single and only just make your ground, or the ball runs past you in the field before you've got going.

why.label: Below target
why.text: You covered 10 metres in {time}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} away.

why.label: At Gold
why.text: You covered 10 metres in {time}. That's Gold level.

tests.fix_it: you'll turn dot balls into quick singles, and cut off balls in the field that used to get past you.

rules.text: Score below tier target → show Fix A: first-step power.
At or above Gold → show Fix B: keep it sharp.

A.title: first-step power
exercises: Falling starts over 5 metres: 6 reps, full rest.
Backing-up starts: walk in with the bowler, then sprint 10 metres on a call. 6 reps.
Split squats: 3 sets of 8 each leg.

B.title: keep it sharp
exercises: Reaction starts over 5 metres on a partner's call: 6 reps.

court_drills: Quick singles: run one at full pace with your bat, grounding it over the line. 6 reps.
Attack the ball: a partner rolls the ball towards you; sprint in, pick up and throw at the stumps. 8 reps.

weapon.headline: Quick off the mark
weapon.body: you are quick over the first few steps

tests.name: 20m Sprint
tests.what_we_measured: How fast you cover 20 metres from a standing start, about the length of the pitch.
tests.nickname: Speed: one run, crease to crease
tests.notice: a two becomes a one because the second run is too tight, or you chase a ball to the rope and it beats you.

why.label: Below target
why.text: You covered 20 metres in {time}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} away.

why.label: At Gold
why.text: You covered 20 metres in {time}. That's Gold level.

tests.fix_it: you'll run more twos, take on more fielders, and stop more boundaries.

rules.text: Score below tier target → show Fix A: build top speed.
At or above Gold → show Fix B: keep it sharp.

A.title: build top speed
exercises: Flying sprints: build up over 10 metres, then sprint 20 metres. 5 reps, full rest.
A-skips: 3 sets of 20 metres.
Hill or incline sprints over 15 metres: 5 reps.

B.title: keep it sharp
exercises: Flying 20-metre sprints: 4 reps, full rest.

court_drills: Run twos: run two at full pace with your bat, turning hard at the far crease. 5 reps.
Chase to the rope: a partner hits the ball past you; chase it and return it. 6 reps.

weapon.headline: Quick between the wickets
weapon.body: you cover the length of the pitch fast

tests.name: 5-0-5 Agility Test
tests.what_we_measured: How quickly you sprint, stop, turn 180° and sprint back out, like turning at the crease.
tests.nickname: Agility: your turn at the crease
tests.notice: a run-out comes down to how fast you turned for the second run, or you overrun the ball in the field and have to come back for it.

why.label: Below target
why.text: You turned and came back in {time}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} away.

why.label: At Gold
why.text: You turned and came back in {time}. That's Gold level.

tests.fix_it: you'll win the tight run-outs, for and against, and get to more balls in the field on balance.

rules.text: Time slower than tier target → show Fix A: brake and turn.
At or above Gold → show Fix B: keep it sharp.

A.title: brake and turn
exercises: Deceleration drills: sprint 5 metres, stop in two steps and hold. 6 reps.
5-0-5 practice at 80% effort, focusing on a low turn: 6 reps.
Lateral lunges: 3 sets of 8 each side.

B.title: keep it sharp
exercises: 5-0-5 turns at full effort, both directions: 4 reps.

court_drills: Turn for two: run one, turn at the crease with your bat and sprint back. Turn off each foot. 6 reps.
Field and turn: a partner hits the ball just past you; stop, turn, pick up and throw. 8 reps.

tests.name: Medicine Ball Throw
tests.what_we_measured: How far you throw a 4 kg medicine ball from a seated position, using your chest, shoulders and arms.
tests.notice: your throws from the deep need a bounce to reach the keeper, or your shots don't carry as far as you expect.

why.label: Below target
why.text: Your throw scored {score}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} points away.

why.label: At Gold
why.text: Your throw scored {score}. That's Gold level.

tests.fix_it: you'll throw flatter and further from the deep, and get more carry on your shots.

rules.text: Score below tier target → show Fix A: build upper-body power.
At or above Gold → show Fix B: maintain.

A.title: build upper-body power
exercises: Medicine ball chest passes against a wall: 3 sets of 8.
Press-ups, slow on the way down: 3 sets of 8.
Medicine ball overhead throws against a wall: 3 sets of 6.

B.title: maintain
exercises: Medicine ball chest passes: 2 sets of 8, once a week.

court_drills: Long throws to the keeper from the edge of the circle, flat and on target: 10 throws.
Medicine ball side throws against a wall: 3 sets of 6 each side.

weapon.headline: A strong arm from the deep

tests.name: Ruler Drop Test
tests.what_we_measured: How far a dropped ruler falls before you catch it. Shorter is faster.
tests.nickname: Reaction: how fast your hands move
tests.notice: a sharp chance in the slips or at short leg is past you before your hands move, or a ball that keeps low catches you late with the bat.

why.label: Below target
why.text: You caught the ruler at {distance}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} away.

why.label: At Gold
why.text: You caught the ruler at {distance}. That's Gold level.

tests.fix_it: you'll hold more close catches and have more time to adjust to late movement with the bat.

rules.text: Catch distance worse than tier target → show Fix A: sharpen reactions.
At or above Gold → show Fix B: keep it sharp.

A.title: sharpen reactions
exercises: Reaction ball against a wall: 3 rounds of 60 seconds.
Partner drops: a partner drops a ball without warning; catch it before the second bounce. 3 sets of 10.

B.title: keep it sharp
exercises: Close catching practice once a week.

court_drills: Slip catching off a partner's edge or a catching cradle: 20 catches.
Short-range reflex catches: a partner throws hard at you from 5 metres. 20 catches.
tests.retest_note: Reaction improves fastest, so it's often the first stat that moves.

tests.name: Single Leg Stand, Eyes Closed
tests.what_we_measured: How steady you stay on one leg with your eyes closed, on each side. This tests the balance system in your ankle and body, not your eyesight.
tests.notice: your front foot lands unsteady in your delivery stride, or you lose your shape after a big stride forward to drive.

why.label: Below target
why.text: With your eyes closed, you held steady for {seconds} seconds. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} away.

why.label: One leg weaker
why.text: Your {weaker_side} leg held steady for {gap}% less time than your other leg.

tests.fix_it: you'll land your delivery stride on balance, stay still at the crease, and protect your ankles and knees.

rules.text: Time held below tier target on either leg → show Fix A: build balance.
One leg holding more than 20% less time than the other (proposed) → also show Fix B: even it out. Ask about past ankle sprains on that side.
rules.coach_note: Ask about past ankle sprains on that side.

A.title: build balance
exercises: Single-leg stands, eyes open then closed: 3 holds of 30 seconds each leg.
Single-leg stands on a cushion or folded towel: 3 holds of 30 seconds each leg.
Single-leg reaches in three directions: 2 sets of 6 each leg.

B.title: even it out
exercises: One extra hold on your weaker leg in every exercise.

court_drills: Front-foot landing holds: walk through your delivery stride and hold the landing for 2 seconds. 3 sets of 6.
Stride and hold: take a full front-foot stride as if driving, and hold for 2 seconds. 3 sets of 6 each side.

weapon.headline: Steady on one leg
weapon.body: you stay steady on one leg with your eyes closed, {evenness}

evenness.even: almost the same on each leg

tests.name: Shoulder External Rotation Strength
tests.what_we_measured: The strength of the muscles at the back of each shoulder that rotate your arm outward.
tests.nickname: Shoulder strength: the brakes on your arm
tests.notice: your throwing or bowling arm gets tired late in a long spell, or your shoulder aches the day after a big fielding session.

why.label: Below target
why.text: Your throwing arm scored {score}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} points away.

why.label: Throwing arm weaker
why.text: Your throwing arm is {gap}% weaker than your other arm. Every throw and every delivery is a fast swing and a hard stop, and the back of the shoulder does the stopping.

tests.fix_it: you can keep bowling and throwing hard all day, and get through a full season with a healthy shoulder.

rules.text: Strength relative to bodyweight below tier target on your throwing arm → show Fix A: strengthen the back of the shoulder.
Throwing arm more than 10% weaker than the other arm (proposed) → also show Fix B: close the gap.
Strong and balanced → show Fix C: maintain.

A.title: strengthen the back of the shoulder
exercises: Side-lying external rotation with a light dumbbell: 3 sets of 12–15.
Band external rotation with the arm at shoulder height (90/90): 3 sets of 12.
Prone Y and T raises: 2 sets of 10 in the warm-up.

B.title: close the gap
exercises: One extra set on your throwing arm for each exercise.

C.title: maintain
exercises: Band external rotation, 2 sets of 15, twice a week.

court_drills: Band external rotation before every session and match: 1 set of 15.
Build up throwing distance gradually in practice while you build strength; don't start with full-power throws from the deep.
Stop and tell us if you feel pain in your shoulder or elbow when you bowl or throw; don't play through it.

weapon.headline: A shoulder built for long spells
weapon.body: the back of your shoulders is strong and {evenness}

tests.name: Shoulder Internal Rotation Strength
tests.what_we_measured: The strength of the muscles at the front of each shoulder that rotate your arm inward, the muscles that whip your arm through.
tests.notice: your throws lose pace once you're tired, or your bowling feels like it's all effort and no zip.

why.label: Below target
why.text: Your shoulders scored {score}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} points away.

why.label: One side weaker
why.text: Your {weaker_side} shoulder is {gap}% weaker than your other shoulder.

tests.fix_it: you'll put more speed on your throws and deliveries, with the strength to back it up.

rules.text: Strength relative to bodyweight below tier target → show Fix A: build arm speed strength.
One side more than 10% weaker than the other (proposed) → also show Fix B: close the gap.
Strong and even → show Fix C: maintain.

A.title: build arm speed strength
exercises: Band internal rotation with the elbow at your side: 3 sets of 12 each arm.
Band internal rotation with the arm at shoulder height (90/90): 3 sets of 10.
Medicine ball chest passes against a wall: 3 sets of 8.

B.title: close the gap
exercises: One extra set on your weaker side for each exercise.

C.title: maintain
exercises: Band internal rotation, 2 sets of 15, twice a week.

court_drills: Short-range throws at one stump, building speed: 3 sets of 8.
Underarm flicks at the stumps from 10 metres: 10 throws.
tests.retest_note: Read this alongside Shoulder External Rotation: the balance between the two matters as much as either number.

weapon.headline: Zip through the arm
weapon.body: the front of your shoulders is strong and {evenness}

tests.name: Elbow Extension Strength
tests.what_we_measured: The strength of the muscles at the back of each upper arm that straighten your elbow.
tests.nickname: Arm strength: the push through the ball
tests.notice: your arm feels heavy late in a spell, or your throws and punches off the back foot lack snap.

why.label: Below target
why.text: Your arms scored {score}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} points away.

why.label: One side weaker
why.text: Your {weaker_side} arm is {gap}% weaker than your other arm.

tests.fix_it: you'll keep your action strong through a long spell and put more snap into throws and back-foot shots.

rules.text: Strength relative to bodyweight below tier target → show Fix A: build arm strength.
One side more than 10% weaker than the other (proposed) → also show Fix B: close the gap.
Strong and even → show Fix C: maintain.

A.title: build arm strength
exercises: Close-grip press-ups: 3 sets of 8.
Band triceps pushdowns: 3 sets of 12.
Overhead band triceps extensions: 3 sets of 12.

B.title: close the gap
exercises: One extra set on your weaker arm for each exercise.

C.title: maintain
exercises: Close-grip press-ups, 2 sets of 10, twice a week.

court_drills: Back-foot punch drives off throwdowns: 3 sets of 8.
Stop and tell us if you feel pain on the inside of your elbow when you bowl or throw; don't play through it.

weapon.headline: Snap through the ball
weapon.body: the backs of your arms are strong and {evenness}

tests.name: Hip Extension Strength
tests.what_we_measured: The strength of your glutes and the back of each hip that drive your leg backward.
tests.nickname: Hip strength: your drive from the ground
tests.notice: your run-up feels like hard work without much pace at the crease, or you lack push-off when you sprint between the wickets.

why.label: Below target
why.text: Your hips scored {score}. {next_tier} starts at {target}, so you're {gap} points away.

why.label: One side weaker
why.text: Your {weaker_side} side is {gap}% weaker than your other side.

tests.fix_it: you'll get more drive into your run-up and delivery, faster running between the wickets, and a stronger, safer lower back.

rules.text: Strength relative to bodyweight below tier target → show Fix A: build hip drive.
One side more than 10% weaker than the other (proposed) → also show Fix B: close the gap.
Strong and even → show Fix C: maintain.

A.title: build hip drive
exercises: Glute bridges, holding for 2 seconds at the top: 3 sets of 12.
Single-leg glute bridges: 3 sets of 8 each leg.
Romanian deadlifts with light dumbbells: 3 sets of 10.

B.title: close the gap
exercises: One extra set of each exercise on the weaker side.

C.title: maintain
exercises: Single-leg glute bridges, 2 sets of 10 each leg, twice a week.

court_drills: Run-up drives: the first 6 strides of your run-up, driving hard off the ground. 6 reps.
Bounding over 20 metres, pushing hard off each leg: 4 reps.
